newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana calls for cellular network tenders.
newsitem.headline: Botswana calls for cellular network tenders.

text.p: The Botswana Telecommunications Authority (BTA) has called for tenders for the establishment of a cellular telephone network, a government spokesman said on Thursday.
Applications will close on August 7 and two licences are to be awarded, the spokesman said.

"Each applicant must show that it is a partnership which includes a citizen or citizens (of Botswana) and has the necessary technical expertise, which will, we accept, have to come from a foreign company," he said.
"The two successful tenderers will each have to pay one million pula (US$ 280,000 - R1,250,000) for a 15 year licence."
Botswana Telecommunications Corporation (BTC) spokesman Mogomotsi Kaboeamodimo confirmed that the corporation intended to apply for a licence and was seeking a partner.
South African cellular service providers Vodacom and MTN linked with BTC recently to provide a temporary service at an international conference in northern Botswana.
The BTA has tried as far as possible to ensure the network will cover a large part of this vast, mostly desert, country.

"The minimum requirements are that both operators will have to establish a network that covers a mandatory section along the line of rail and main road from Lobatse in the south to Francistown in the north," the BTA spokesman said.
"One licence holder will then have to add coverage of the trans-Kalahari highway, and the other the northern tourist areas of Maun and Kasane. Both networks will have to be accessible to all users."

There are 60,000 fixed line telephone subscribers in Botswana. The initial cellular market was estimated by a BTC executive recently at around 10,000, rising over 10 years to between 50,000 and 60,000.
